reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through Oct 30: SPX 7,580.07, down 3.37% from its 120-day high, 1.52% below its 50-day but still 3.7% above its 200-day (7,309.76); SMH 522.49, down 22.23% from its high and between zones; NVDA 204.64 inside Zone 1; VIX 19.42 at its 5-day high with no rollover; HY OAS 3.26, credit calm; mechanical capitulation tally 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: A close above SPX 7,820 with SMH reclaiming $600 and HY OAS under 4% proves the correction is over without a Zone 2 print — the Watch stance and the Zone 2 ladder are void, and waiting cost the entry. Conversely, HY OAS above 4% voids the probe plan entirely.

ladder.response: Probe the first tranche — small size only, per the deployment ladder; this is a probe, not an all-in.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes into Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA into $175–185 with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

ladder.response: Do not chase; treat as the bull trap — hold cash and wait for the retest verdict before any probe.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone (SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820) that stalls or reverses

ladder.response: Stand down — halt all probing and hold bills; the regime has broken, not bottomed.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Reassess the ladder — no adds until a second low holds; the 7,300 zone becomes the next decision line.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day (~$7,310) with SMH below Zone 2

ladder.response: Re-enter: add per the ladder — the bottom is confirmed, not guessed.
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds with the 10-year falling — or SPX closing above $7,750–7,820 with SMH reclaiming $600

reaction.trapRisk: SMH fell 6.98% on Oct 30 on 1.99x average volume with the close in only 46% of its range, and VIX sits at its 5-day high with no rollover — the tape has not yet printed a capitulation reversal, so the first bounce is the most likely to fail. Entries change accordingly: no chasing the first bounce, no sizing before the failure-zone retest (SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820) delivers its verdict, and any probe waits for the tally to reach 3 of 4.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real but the bottom is unconfirmed: the mechanical tally is 2 of 4, NVDA is inside Zone 1 at $204.64 but SMH is still between zones at $522.49, and VIX sits at its 5-day high with no rollover. No new money until Zone 2 or a confirmed tally, and no chasing the first bounce.

themes.counterRead: Leadership is rotating, not collapsing — but the divergence itself is real and worth tracking, because credit conditions can flip. If lending standards tighten or HY OAS breaks above 4%, the rotation read dies and the rollover read takes over.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag7 average sits 16% below its 52-week highs while SPY is only 3.3% below its own — a 12.7-point divergence gap. The index itself is down just 3.37% from its 120-day high (SPX 7,580.07 on Oct 30), still 3.7% above its 200-day (7,309.76). Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), and HY OAS is 3.26 and calm. The weakest Mag7 name is GOOGL at -31.5% from its high; the strongest is AAPL at -2%.
themes.label: Mag7 unwind: rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market rollover: the names that carried the index are falling hard, with GOOGL down 16.7% in a month and META down 15.4%.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS moving off 0% toward stress territory.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression, not demand collapse, is doing the damage — NVDA's dislocation reason is MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, MU's is an acute catalyst. That is the setup for a DATA_AHEAD read, but it is not a buy signal yet: NVDA is in Zone 1, SMH is still between zones at $522.49, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4. The opportunity is real; the entry is not yet confirmed.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA is the top conviction promotion (score 83): revenue growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 15.9% below its high at $204.64, RSI 35.1. AVGO (score 81, tier A): revenue up 55% year over year, 67.8% gross margin, free cash flow of $26,914M at a 42.1% margin — while 34.1% below its high. LRCX: revenue up 131.3% year over year, 45.5% below its high. DDOG: revenue up 27.7%, 80% gross margin, 21.8% below its high. SMH is down 22.23% from its high and NVDA sits inside Zone 1 ($200–210), not Zone 2.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is a financing trade that cannot bottom until the funding channel clears — chip and infrastructure names are priced as if demand is rolling over.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing into Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA into $175–185 with the tally at 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: The insider buying at VST and NXT's relative strength say the trough may be forming for the contracted-cash-flow names, but the pre-revenue story names (SMR, OKLO) have no such anchor. Do not treat the whole complex as one trade: contracted cash flow versus pre-revenue story is the split that matters.
themes.dataAnchor: The complex fell 12–30% in a month: SMR -27.6%, OKLO -29.77%, URA -13.42%, GEV -12.25%. VST sits 29.7% below its high at $138.37 with revenue flagged DETERIORATING, though insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. NXT is the exception — up 3.8% in the month and the only 1-month leader in the complex — but still 51.4% below its high.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the story ran ahead of the cash flow
themes.narrative: Nuclear power was the AI trade's second leg — contracted demand from hyperscalers justified any price for SMR, OKLO and the uranium complex.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above its trough with a second insider print, or SMR/OKLO stabilizing while uranium (URA) stops falling.

themes.counterRead: This is the tape doing what it is supposed to do in a correction — the most levered, most narrative-driven names fall first and hardest. It confirms the episode is a genuine risk-off move, not a rotation artifact. It also means the bottoming signal, when it comes, will show up here first: watch for these names stabilizing before the index does.
themes.dataAnchor: CONL is down 47.38% in a month (-24.15% on the day), RDDT down 38.77% in a month and 65.2% below its high with RSI 17.5, COIN down 25.53% in a month (-12.22% on the day), BMNR down 23.61%, TQQQ down 19.87% in a month (-8.91% on the day), ASTS down 28.66%, RKLB down 21.87%. QQQ itself is down 6.37% in a month and 2.88% on the day.
themes.label: Leveraged and crypto-adjacent blowout
themes.narrative: The speculative fringe is being liquidated: leveraged ETFs and crypto-adjacent names are in free fall as risk appetite drains.
themes.watchFor: CONL, RDDT or COIN putting in a higher low while QQQ stops making new lows.

themes.counterRead: Bonds are rallying on fear, not on a dovish Fed — the December FOMC (Dec 8–9) is still an anticipated HIGH-signal event, and the October FOMC remains active in the news flow. If the 10-year breaks back above 5.2% with HY OAS widening, the calm read breaks with it. For now, credit is the permission slip that keeps this a correction rather than a regime break.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.98% — below the 5.2% bond-regime falsifier line — with the 2-year at 4.61% and the curve at +0.37 (2s10s), steepening rather than inverting further. The Fed funds rate is 3.88%, the real 10-year is 2.64%, and HY OAS is 3.26 with credit flagged calm, not cracking. VIX is 19.42, up 26.85% over the month but still below the 25 stand-down line.
themes.label: Credit and rates calm while equities stress
themes.narrative: Rates are the pressure valve: the 10-year near 5% and a hawkish Fed are supposed to be choking the market, with the October FOMC and the December meeting looming.
themes.watchFor: 10-year closing above 5.2% or HY OAS above 4%.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes at the Zone 2 test — SMH $470–505 / NVDA $175–185 — or in the trap direction, a bounce into the failure zone (SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820) that stalls. This week decides which: midterms on Nov 3, Apple and Palantir earnings, and the jobs report on Nov 6 are the catalysts on the tape.
